data.summary: ddflow tests --item selects ~300 files (nearly the whole suite) when a touched module is imported transitively by ddflow.config, so the selection is no cheaper than the full run; needs a depth cap or direct-importers-only mode

chunk_findings.detail:
Merging `new_file_globs` into the `shared` list used by `overlaps` exempts the *whole pattern* from lease-overlap checks, not just staged new files. `is_shared(mine, shared)` is true for any claim whose glob matches `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/*.toml` — including a claim of an **existing** fragment or even of the pattern itself. That lets an agent take a lease over a path that is currently covered by another agent's live lease, and `_uncovered_paths(paths, mine, shared)` in enforce.py then treats an edit to that file as "inside a glob I hold", so the commit hook does not block it (the new-file filter only removes added paths, so edits are irrelevant here).

Concrete failure: agent B has committed `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.foo.bar.toml` and holds a live lease covering it. Agent A declares/claims the glob `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.foo.bar.toml` (or the pattern `.../unreleased/*.toml`). In `overlaps` the live check against B is skipped because `new_file_globs` is in `shared`, so A's lease is granted; A then stages a modification (or deletion) of B's existing fragment, which is inside A's own lease, so enforce returns `OK` and B's fragment is silently overwritten. This directly contradicts the contract written for the knob in `config_sections/lease.py`: "An EDIT, rename or delete of an existing file still needs a lease that covers it: another agent's fragment stays theirs." The admission side should distinguish non-existent (new) paths from existing ones, or the commit side must reject edits covered only by a self-granted `new_file_globs` lease.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/admission.py:102 (`overlaps`, `shared = [*shared_globs(cfg), *new_file_globs(cfg)]`)

chunk_findings.detail: The exemption introduced for `[lease] new_file_globs` is applied at pattern granularity, not at file granularity, and this change does not address it. Concrete failure: agent A is already holding a lease on `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/x.toml` (or on the directory pattern itself). Agent B attempts to claim the same path. `overlaps()` computes `shared` by merging `new_file_globs(cfg)` into the list, so `is_shared(mine, shared)` returns true for *any* claim whose glob matches `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/*.toml` — not only for a file B is about to create. No overlap is reported, so B is granted a lease over a path A is actively holding, and `_uncovered_paths(paths, mine, shared)` in enforce.py treats those paths as covered, so the collision is never surfaced at write time either. At claim time there is no "new file" yet, so the pattern must not be blanket-shared; the exemption needs to be scoped to files that are actually being added (as the merge.py side now does via `diff_filter="A"`, whose exemption is correctly limited to the added set) or to paths not currently under a live lease. The merge-side change in this diff does not answer this finding, and the triage left it untriaged, so it still holds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/admission.py:102 (`overlaps`: `shared = [*shared_globs(cfg), *new_file_globs(cfg)]`)

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds, and the prose added in this hunk makes the contradiction explicit rather than answering it. The earlier finding quoted the live code in `overlaps`: `shared = [*shared_globs(cfg), *new_file_globs(cfg)]`, and `is_shared(claim, shared)` is true for *anything* inside `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/*.toml`, not only for a staged new file. Concretely: agent B holds a live lease on `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.a.b.toml` (or on the directory pattern `.../unreleased/*.toml`). Agent A then claims the very same path/pattern; `overlaps` treats A's claim as "shared" and reports no conflict, so A acquires a lease over a path that is currently covered by B's live lease. Because A now holds that glob, `_uncovered_paths(paths, mine, shared)` in `services/enforce.py` treats edits of B's *existing* fragment as covered by `mine`, so A's edit of `unreleased/knob_added.a.b.toml` commits — exactly the "another agent's fragment stays theirs" guarantee the change is supposed to keep. The new `_without_new_files` helper does not answer this: it only drops paths staged with status `A` from the uncovered list, and it runs *after* `_uncovered_paths`, whose `mine` argument is already the overlapping lease. Worse, the new text asserts the opposite of the code — `config_sections/lease.py` says "claim globs are unaffected, so a lease you do take stays exclusive", and `admission.new_file_globs` says "Never exempt from lease overlap (a lease on an existing fragment stays exclusive)" — while line 102 still feeds `new_file_globs` into the shared list consulted by `overlaps`. The triage is "untriaged" and no fix/probe was supplied, so nothing refutes the original scenario; the exemption needs to be restricted to genuinely new staged paths (matching the file's own status, e.g. `A`) rather than to the whole pattern at claim time, or the two docstrings must be corrected to admit directory/fragment claims are non-exclusive.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/admission.py:102 (`overlaps`, `shared = [*shared_globs(cfg), *new_file_globs(cfg)]`)

chunk_findings.detail: The prior finding is untriaged and nothing in this part of the diff answers it — this part actually *supplies the default that makes it reachable*. The fragment adds `lease.new_file_globs = ["ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/*.toml"]`, and `overlaps()` builds `shared = [*shared_globs(cfg), *new_file_globs(cfg)]`, so the whole pattern `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/*.toml` is treated as shared/exempt rather than only staged-new files. Concretely: agent A holds a live lease on an *existing* fragment it is editing, e.g. `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.foo.toml`; agent B claims that same path; because B's claim matches a `new_file_globs` pattern that has been folded into `shared`, the overlap check is skipped and `_uncovered_paths` in enforce.py no longer flags it, so B gets a colliding lease over a path another agent already holds. That directly contradicts the doc text this same diff adds to the golden snapshot ("An EDIT, rename or delete of an existing file still needs a lease that covers it: another agent's fragment stays theirs" / "claim globs are unaffected, so a lease you do take stays exclusive"). Either the merge into `shared` must be dropped (new-file exemption applied only to genuinely new/untracked paths) or the `*.toml` pattern must not be in `shared`; as written the new default widens lease collisions over existing fragments.

chunk_findings.detail: This is the earlier-reported finding, still untriaged and not answered by the diff under review. The diff (part 5 of 8) only updates the golden transcript `tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json` to reflect the new knob `lease.new_file_globs = ['ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/*.toml']   [default]`; it does not touch the admission/enforce code path where `new_file_globs` is folded into the `shared` list used by `overlaps`. Because the pattern is propagated into `is_shared(mine, shared)` as a whole glob (not evaluated only against staged/uncommitted files), a claim whose path matches `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/*.toml` is treated as shared even when it targets an already-existing fragment owned by another agent's live lease — e.g. agent A holds a lease on `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob-a.toml`, agent B claims the same existing file, `is_shared` returns true, no overlap is reported, and the same `shared` set flows into `_uncovered_paths(paths, mine, shared)` in enforce.py so the second writer's commit is not flagged. Exempting new files is the intent; exempting the entire pattern (including existing fragments) is the over-broad part the finding describes, and nothing in the shown diff narrows it.

chunk_findings.detail:
This fixture ships the knob's `doc` claiming the exemption is narrow and claim-neutral:
"A NEW file matching one of these needs no glob of its own beyond holding some live lease
(the commit hook covers it; **claim globs are unaffected, so a lease you do take stays
exclusive**), so two tasks adding different knobs never collide on the directory. An EDIT,
rename or delete of an existing file still needs a lease that covers it: another agent's
fragment stays theirs." The earlier review reported that `overlaps`
(`ddflow/core/admission.py:102`) instead does `shared = [*shared_globs(cfg),
*new_file_globs(cfg)]`, i.e. it folds `new_file_globs` into the *shared* list. Under that
mechanism `is_shared(mine, shared)` is true for **any** claim whose glob matches
`ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/*.toml` — a claim of an existing fragment, or of the
pattern itself — so claims *are* affected and a lease on an existing fragment taken by
another agent would no longer block (and `_uncovered_paths(..., shared)` in enforce.py
would treat it as covered). That directly contradicts the sentence this fixture now
records as the knob's contract. The triage is `untriaged` and this part of the diff touches
no code (`admission.py`, `enforce.py` are absent), so nothing here fixes or refutes it: the
fixture and the implementation disagree, and one of the two has to change.

chunk_findings.detail: The only thing this part of the change does is regenerate the `--explain` golden transcript so it carries the new `lease.new_file_globs = ['ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/*.toml']` knob and its help text. Nothing here (and nothing in the shipped help text) restricts the exemption to files that do **not** exist yet, so the earlier finding still holds. The help text this change now ships promises "claim globs are unaffected, so a lease you do take stays exclusive" and "An EDIT, rename or delete of an existing file still needs a lease that covers it: another agent's fragment stays theirs". That is exactly what merging the new-file globs into the `shared` list used by `overlaps` cannot deliver: `is_shared(mine, shared)` matches any claim whose path matches `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/*.toml`, including a claim of an existing fragment or of the directory glob itself. Concretely: agent A claims the existing fragment `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.shared_globs.toml`; agent B claims the same exact path (or `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/*.toml`); because that path matches the new-file glob it is treated as shared, `overlaps` returns nothing, both live leases stand on one file, and `_uncovered_paths(paths, mine, shared)` likewise treats it as covered — so B can edit, rename or delete A's fragment under a lease that the documentation says does not cover an existing file. The regression-test/transcript update in this diff does not answer the finding, because it changes no admission behavior; the exemption still needs to be keyed on "the staged path is a new file" (as the knob name and its own text say) rather than on the whole pattern.

The only content in this part of the diff is the `config --explain` transcript fixture, which adds the new `lease.new_file_globs` entry and its doc text — it makes no change to the admission code that was flagged. The new knob's own documentation states the intended semantics: "claim globs are unaffected, so a lease you do take stays exclusive" and "An EDIT, rename or delete of an existing file still needs a lease that covers it: another agent's fragment stays theirs."
